name: Advanced Tuck Front Lever
index_description: From tuck position, extend your knees slightly while keeping thighs close to chest. Maintain horizontal torso position.

steps.name: Set up
steps.text: Hang from a pull-up bar with overhand grip. Start in tuck front lever position.

steps.name: Create a stable start
steps.text: Use an overhand grip, depress the shoulder blades, and establish a hollow trunk before extending the hips.

steps.name: Perform the movement
steps.text: From tuck position, extend your knees slightly while keeping thighs close to chest. Maintain horizontal torso position.

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Hold only while the hips remain level with the shoulders, then return with control rather than dropping.

instructions:
1. Set up: Hang from a pull-up bar with overhand grip. Start in tuck front lever position.
2. Create a stable start: Use an overhand grip, depress the shoulder blades, and establish a hollow trunk before extending the hips.
3. Perform the movement: From tuck position, extend your knees slightly while keeping thighs close to chest. Maintain horizontal torso position.
4. Finish with control: Hold only while the hips remain level with the shoulders, then return with control rather than dropping.
coaching_cues: Push the bar toward your hips
Shorten the lever before form breaks
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows
Letting the hips sag
Losing the hollow trunk position
Choosing a progression that cannot be held cleanly
easier_variations: Front-lever row in a short lever

programming.Strength: Use 3-5 sets of controlled, challenging work and stop before technique changes.
programming.Muscle and work capacity: Use 2-4 sets in a repeatable range, adding reps before adding load or difficulty.
programming.Skill and control: Practice low-fatigue sets early in the session with full rest between attempts.

full_description: Advanced Tuck Front Lever is a advanced calisthenics exercise for straight-arm pulling strength and whole-body tension. The source muscle map identifies Latissimus Dorsi, Rectus Abdominis, Deltoid Posterior Head as the primary targets.

name: Advanced Tuck Planche
index_description: Hold position with knees bent but hips more extended than tuck planche. Maintain straight arms and forward lean.

steps.name: Enter a tuck planche
steps.text: Start from a solid tuck planche.

steps.name: Flatten the back
steps.text: Open the hips so the back is flat and parallel to the floor, keeping the knees bent.

steps.name: Increase the lean
steps.text: Lean slightly further forward to balance the longer lever.

steps.name: Hold
steps.text: Hold for 5-10 seconds with locked elbows.

instructions:
1. Enter a tuck planche: Start from a solid tuck planche.
2. Flatten the back: Open the hips so the back is flat and parallel to the floor, keeping the knees bent.
3. Increase the lean: Lean slightly further forward to balance the longer lever.
4. Hold: Hold for 5-10 seconds with locked elbows.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping below shoulder height.
Bending the elbows to compensate for a weak lean.

programming.Skill strength: 5-8 sets of 5-12 second holds at the hardest progression you can hold with good form, 2 minutes rest, 2-3 times per week.
programming.Volume: Accumulate 30-60 seconds of total good-quality hold time per session, split into short sets.
programming.Progression rule: Move to the next progression when you can do 3 sets of 10-15 seconds with perfect form.

full_description: The advanced tuck planche flattens the back so the hips are level with the shoulders and the knees move away from the chest. That lengthens the lever compared with the tuck planche and demands more forward lean. It is usually the longest plateau in planche training.

name: Alternating Dumbbell Press
index_description: Lower one dumbbell to chest while keeping the other extended. Press back up and repeat with opposite arm in alternating fashion.

steps.name: Set up
steps.text: Lie on bench with dumbbells in both hands. Position dumbbells over chest with arms extended.

steps.name: Create a stable start
steps.text: Set the bench and feet firmly, bring the dumbbell or dumbbells into position, and brace before pressing.

steps.name: Perform the movement
steps.text: Lower one dumbbell to chest while keeping the other extended. Press back up and repeat with opposite arm in alternating fashion.

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Stack the weight over the shoulder without forcefully clashing the dumbbells or losing rib position.

instructions:
1. Set up: Lie on bench with dumbbells in both hands. Position dumbbells over chest with arms extended.
2. Create a stable start: Set the bench and feet firmly, bring the dumbbell or dumbbells into position, and brace before pressing.
3. Perform the movement: Lower one dumbbell to chest while keeping the other extended. Press back up and repeat with opposite arm in alternating fashion.
4. Finish with control: Stack the weight over the shoulder without forcefully clashing the dumbbells or losing rib position.
common_mistakes: Using an unstable foot position
Dropping too quickly into the bottom
Flaring the elbows beyond a comfortable path
Turning the press into a whole-body heave

name: Archer Pull-Up
index_description: Pull yourself up while shifting your weight to one side, keeping the opposite arm straight as you pull to one hand

steps.name: Take a wide grip
steps.text: Grip the bar about 1.5-2 times shoulder width with an overhand grip.

steps.name: Choose a side
steps.text: From an active hang, start pulling toward the right hand while keeping the left arm long.

steps.name: Pull to the working hand
steps.text: Bring the chin to the right hand. The left arm ends almost straight along the bar.

steps.name: Lower and switch
steps.text: Lower to the centre and full hang, then pull to the other side. Alternate or do all reps on one side first.

instructions:
1. Take a wide grip: Grip the bar about 1.5-2 times shoulder width with an overhand grip.
2. Choose a side: From an active hang, start pulling toward the right hand while keeping the left arm long.
3. Pull to the working hand: Bring the chin to the right hand. The left arm ends almost straight along the bar.
4. Lower and switch: Lower to the centre and full hang, then pull to the other side. Alternate or do all reps on one side first.
common_mistakes: Bending the 'straight' arm so it becomes a wide pull-up.
Twisting the torso to reach the hand.
Trying archers before 10+ strict pull-ups.
easier_variations: Wide-Grip Pull-up:Build wide-grip strength with both arms.
Typewriter pull-up:Pull to the top, then shift side to side without lowering.
harder_variations: Assisted one-arm pull-up:Hold a towel or band with the free hand.
One-arm negative:Lower slowly with one arm.

programming.Strength: 4-5 sets of 3-5 reps per side, 2-3 minutes rest.
programming.Volume: 3 sets of 5-6 per side, twice a week.
programming.Balance: Start with your weaker side each session.

full_description: In an archer pull-up you take a wide grip, pull toward one hand, and keep the other arm nearly straight along the bar. The straight arm still helps, but much less than in a normal pull-up, so the bent arm carries most of your weight. It is a standard stepping stone toward one-arm pull-ups.

name: Archer Push-Up
index_description: Lower your body while shifting weight to one side, keeping one arm bent and the other relatively straight. Push back up and alternate sides.

steps.name: Set a wide base
steps.text: Place the hands about twice shoulder width, fingers pointing forward or slightly out.

steps.name: Shift and lower
steps.text: Shift the chest toward the right hand, bending the right elbow while the left arm straightens.

steps.name: Press back
steps.text: Press through the right hand back to the centre.

steps.name: Alternate
steps.text: Repeat to the left, or do all reps on one side first.

instructions:
1. Set a wide base: Place the hands about twice shoulder width, fingers pointing forward or slightly out.
2. Shift and lower: Shift the chest toward the right hand, bending the right elbow while the left arm straightens.
3. Press back: Press through the right hand back to the centre.
4. Alternate: Repeat to the left, or do all reps on one side first.
common_mistakes: Bending the 'straight' arm so it becomes a wide push-up.
Rotating the hips toward the floor.
Stopping well short of the working hand.
easier_variations: Staggered Push-up:One hand forward of the other.
harder_variations: Archer push-up with a pause:More time on the working arm.

programming.Strength: 4-5 sets of 5-8 reps using a variation hard enough that 8 is close to your limit; 2 minutes rest.
programming.Muscle growth: 3-4 sets of 8-20 reps close to failure, 2-3 times per week, counting toward roughly 10+ weekly sets for the chest and triceps.
programming.Endurance and testing: 1-2 sets of maximum strict reps once every 2-3 weeks to track progress.

full_description: An archer push-up uses a very wide hand position: as you lower, you shift toward one hand while the other arm straightens out to the side. The bent arm carries most of your weight, making archers a key step toward the one-arm push-up.

name: Assisted Pull-Up (Machine)
index_description: Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar, then lower yourself back down with control while the machine assists

steps.name: Set the assistance
steps.text: Select a counterweight that lets you do 8-10 controlled reps. A common starting point is 30-50% of bodyweight.

steps.name: Mount the machine
steps.text: Step onto the platform, grip the handles overhand at shoulder width, and lower the platform with your knees or feet.

steps.name: Start from straight arms
steps.text: Let the arms fully straighten, then pull the shoulders down away from the ears.

steps.name: Pull to the bar
steps.text: Drive the elbows down until the chin is over the handles.

steps.name: Lower under control
steps.text: Lower over 2-3 seconds. The machine should not throw you back down.

instructions:
1. Set the assistance: Select a counterweight that lets you do 8-10 controlled reps. A common starting point is 30-50% of bodyweight.
2. Mount the machine: Step onto the platform, grip the handles overhand at shoulder width, and lower the platform with your knees or feet.
3. Start from straight arms: Let the arms fully straighten, then pull the shoulders down away from the ears.
4. Pull to the bar: Drive the elbows down until the chin is over the handles.
5. Lower under control: Lower over 2-3 seconds. The machine should not throw you back down.
coaching_cues: Drop the stack a notch each week
common_mistakes: Using so much assistance that the set feels easy and nothing improves.
Stopping short of straight arms at the bottom.
Never reducing the assistance from week to week.
easier_variations: Lat pulldown:Builds the same pattern seated.
Inverted row:Horizontal pulling with feet on the floor.
harder_variations: Negative Pull-up:Practise the unassisted lowering phase.

programming.Progression: 3-4 sets of 6-10 reps. When all sets hit 10 reps, reduce the assistance by one plate (about 5 kg).
programming.Muscle growth: 3-4 sets of 8-12 reps close to failure, 2-3 times per week.
programming.Bridging to strict reps: Once assistance is under 15-20% of bodyweight, add one strict-rep attempt at the start of each session.

full_description: An assisted pull-up machine uses a counterweight under a knee or foot platform to reduce how much of your bodyweight you lift. On most machines, more weight on the stack means more help. Because the assistance is constant and easy to adjust in small steps, it is the most measurable way to progress toward a strict pull-up.

name: Band Push-up
index_description: Lower chest toward floor against band resistance, then push back up fighting increased resistance at top of movement.

steps.name: Set up
steps.text: Place resistance band across upper back, holding ends in hands. Assume push-up position with band providing additional resistance.

steps.name: Create a stable start
steps.text: Place the hands securely, spread the fingers, and establish a rigid line through the head, ribs, pelvis, and legs.

steps.name: Perform the movement
steps.text: Lower chest toward floor against band resistance, then push back up fighting increased resistance at top of movement.

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Press the floor away until the elbows are straight without letting the hips sag or lead the movement.

instructions:
1. Set up: Place resistance band across upper back, holding ends in hands. Assume push-up position with band providing additional resistance.
2. Create a stable start: Place the hands securely, spread the fingers, and establish a rigid line through the head, ribs, pelvis, and legs.
3. Perform the movement: Lower chest toward floor against band resistance, then push back up fighting increased resistance at top of movement.
4. Finish with control: Press the floor away until the elbows are straight without letting the hips sag or lead the movement.
coaching_cues: Screw the hands into the floor
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows excessively
Letting the hips sag
Shortening depth as fatigue rises
Leading with the chin

programming.Muscle and work capacity: Use 2-4 sets in a repeatable range, adding reps before adding load or difficulty.

full_description: Band Push-up is a intermediate chest exercise for horizontal pressing strength with trunk control. The source muscle map identifies Pectoralis Major, Triceps Brachii Lateral Long, Deltoid Anterior Head as the primary targets.

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
index_description: Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar, using the band's assistance, then lower with control

steps.name: Anchor the band
steps.text: Loop the band around the bar and pull one end through the other so it cinches tight in the middle of the bar.

steps.name: Step in safely
steps.text: Use a box to place one foot (more help) or one knee (less leverage, slightly less help) into the band.

steps.name: Hang and set
steps.text: Grip overhand at shoulder width, step off the box, and let the band take your weight with arms straight.

steps.name: Pull and lower
steps.text: Pull until the chin clears the bar, then lower in 2-3 seconds to straight arms without letting the band bounce you.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band: Loop the band around the bar and pull one end through the other so it cinches tight in the middle of the bar.
2. Step in safely: Use a box to place one foot (more help) or one knee (less leverage, slightly less help) into the band.
3. Hang and set: Grip overhand at shoulder width, step off the box, and let the band take your weight with arms straight.
4. Pull and lower: Pull until the chin clears the bar, then lower in 2-3 seconds to straight arms without letting the band bounce you.
common_mistakes: Using the band to bounce out of the bottom.
Letting the band swing the legs forward, which tips the body away from the bar.
Staying on the same band for months instead of progressing.
Losing the top of the pull because the band gives less help there.
easier_variations: Thicker band:More assistance across the range.
harder_variations: Thinner band:Less assistance; progress band by band.
Negative Pull-up:Strengthens the top and middle of the pull unassisted.

programming.Progression: 3-4 sets of 5-8 reps. When you hit 8 reps on all sets, move to the next thinner band.
programming.Top-range strength: Add 2-3 sets of 10-20 second flexed-arm hangs or negatives in the same session.
programming.Frequency: 2-3 sessions per week with at least a day between them.

full_description: A band-assisted pull-up uses a looped resistance band hung from the bar to support part of your bodyweight. The band stretches most at the bottom, where it helps most, and helps least near the top, where it has shortened. That makes it the opposite of most people's strength curve, so it is useful but should be combined with work that strengthens the top of the pull.

name: Band-Resisted Pull-up
index_description: Perform pull-ups against the added resistance of the band, which increases difficulty at the top

steps.name: Set up
steps.text: Attach resistance band to pull-up bar and hang from bar with band providing additional resistance

steps.name: Create a stable start
steps.text: Take a secure grip and begin from a controlled hang with the shoulder blades gently active.

steps.name: Perform the movement
steps.text: Perform pull-ups against the added resistance of the band, which increases difficulty at the top

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Reach the strongest height you can without craning the neck, then return to a full controlled hang.

instructions:
1. Set up: Attach resistance band to pull-up bar and hang from bar with band providing additional resistance
2. Create a stable start: Take a secure grip and begin from a controlled hang with the shoulder blades gently active.
3. Perform the movement: Perform pull-ups against the added resistance of the band, which increases difficulty at the top
4. Finish with control: Reach the strongest height you can without craning the neck, then return to a full controlled hang.
common_mistakes: Kicking to create momentum
Shrugging into a passive bottom position
Reaching with the chin instead of lifting the torso
Dropping through the eccentric

full_description: Band-Resisted Pull-up is a intermediate pull exercise for vertical pulling strength through the back, arms, and shoulder girdle. The source muscle map identifies Latissimus Dorsi, Trapezius as the primary targets.

name: Banded Sit-Up
index_description: Contract your abs and sit up while the band provides assistance or resistance depending on setup. Control the movement in both directions.

steps.name: Anchor the band
steps.text: For resistance, loop the band around a rack or post behind your head at about floor-to-knee height and hold the ends at your shoulders. For assistance, anchor it in front of you at foot level and hold it with both hands.

steps.name: Find the starting tension
steps.text: Shuffle closer to or farther from the anchor so the band is slightly taut at the start. No slack is the goal.

steps.name: Sit up
steps.text: Keep the hands fixed at the shoulders (resisted) or arms straight (assisted) and curl up to an upright position.

steps.name: Resist the return
steps.text: Lower over 2-3 seconds. In the resisted version, do not let the band snap you back to the floor.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band: For resistance, loop the band around a rack or post behind your head at about floor-to-knee height and hold the ends at your shoulders. For assistance, anchor it in front of you at foot level and hold it with both hands.
2. Find the starting tension: Shuffle closer to or farther from the anchor so the band is slightly taut at the start. No slack is the goal.
3. Sit up: Keep the hands fixed at the shoulders (resisted) or arms straight (assisted) and curl up to an upright position.
4. Resist the return: Lower over 2-3 seconds. In the resisted version, do not let the band snap you back to the floor.
coaching_cues: Fight the band on the way down
common_mistakes: Letting the band pull you back quickly so the lowering phase disappears.
Pulling with the arms in the resisted version instead of keeping the hands fixed at the shoulders.
Anchoring to something that can move or roll.
easier_variations: Band-assisted version:Anchor the band in front and use it as a pull to get up.
Incline Sit-up:Bench support instead of band support.
harder_variations: Heavier band:Increase resistance in small steps.
Weighted Sit-up:Constant load through the full range.

programming.Strength: 3-4 sets of 6-10 controlled repetitions with a load that leaves 1-3 repetitions in reserve. Rest 90-120 seconds.
programming.Muscle growth: 2-4 sets of 8-15 repetitions taken close to failure, 2-3 times per week as part of roughly 10+ weekly sets for the trunk flexors.
programming.Technique and tolerance: 2-3 sets of 5-8 slow repetitions with a 3-second lowering phase before adding load or range.

full_description: A banded sit-up uses a resistance band either to help you up or to make the movement harder. Where you anchor the band determines which: a band anchored behind and above your head resists the sit-up, while a band anchored in front of you that you hold onto assists it. Getting the anchor right is the main technical point of this exercise.

name: Barbell Lunges
index_description: Step forward with one leg into lunge position while maintaining barbell position. Lower until both knees reach 90 degrees, then push through front heel to return to start.

steps.name: Set up
steps.text: Position barbell on upper back in squat position, step back from rack, and stand with feet hip-width apart.

steps.name: Create a stable start
steps.text: Choose a stance long enough for both legs to bend comfortably and keep the whole front foot planted.

steps.name: Perform the movement
steps.text: Step forward with one leg into lunge position while maintaining barbell position. Lower until both knees reach 90 degrees, then push through front heel to return to start.

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Drive through the front foot to return without pushing off aggressively from the back leg.

instructions:
1. Set up: Position barbell on upper back in squat position, step back from rack, and stand with feet hip-width apart.
2. Create a stable start: Choose a stance long enough for both legs to bend comfortably and keep the whole front foot planted.
3. Perform the movement: Step forward with one leg into lunge position while maintaining barbell position. Lower until both knees reach 90 degrees, then push through front heel to return to start.
4. Finish with control: Drive through the front foot to return without pushing off aggressively from the back leg.
common_mistakes: Using a stance that is too narrow
Letting the front knee collapse inward
Losing pressure through the front heel
Rushing the bottom range

name: Barbell Squat
index_description: Initiate movement by pushing hips back and bending knees. Descend until thighs are parallel to floor. Drive through heels to return to starting position.

steps.name: Set the rack
steps.text: Set the bar at mid-chest height and the safety pins just below your bottom position.

steps.name: Get under the bar
steps.text: Grip just outside the shoulders. Place the bar on the upper trapezius (high bar) or across the rear deltoids (low bar), squeeze the shoulder blades and lift it out of the rack.

steps.name: Walk out and brace
steps.text: Take two or three short steps back, set the feet at about shoulder width, then breathe into the belly and brace hard.

steps.name: Descend
steps.text: Bend the hips and knees together, keep the bar over the mid-foot, and descend to at least parallel or the deepest depth you control.

steps.name: Drive up
steps.text: Push the floor away, keep the chest and hips rising together, and lock out. Re-brace before the next rep.

instructions:
1. Set the rack: Set the bar at mid-chest height and the safety pins just below your bottom position.
2. Get under the bar: Grip just outside the shoulders. Place the bar on the upper trapezius (high bar) or across the rear deltoids (low bar), squeeze the shoulder blades and lift it out of the rack.
3. Walk out and brace: Take two or three short steps back, set the feet at about shoulder width, then breathe into the belly and brace hard.
4. Descend: Bend the hips and knees together, keep the bar over the mid-foot, and descend to at least parallel or the deepest depth you control.
5. Drive up: Push the floor away, keep the chest and hips rising together, and lock out. Re-brace before the next rep.
common_mistakes: Hips shooting up first so the squat turns into a good morning.
Losing the brace at the bottom.
Knees caving in under load.
Bar drifting forward of the mid-foot.
Squatting heavy without safety pins or a spotter.
easier_variations: Goblet Squat:Front-loaded squat that teaches an upright torso.
Box Squat:Controlled depth with a box.
harder_variations: Pause Squat:Pause at the bottom for strength out of the hole.
Front Squat:Bar in front; more quadriceps and upper-back demand.
Squat with Chains:Accommodating resistance for advanced lifters.

programming.Strength: 3-5 sets of 3-6 reps at a load that leaves 1-3 reps in reserve, 2-3 minutes rest.
programming.Muscle growth: 3-4 sets of 6-12 reps close to failure, 2 sessions per week, counting toward roughly 10+ weekly sets for the legs.
programming.Technique: 2-3 sets of 5 reps at a light load with a 3-second descent, at the start of the session.

full_description: The barbell back squat places a loaded bar across the upper back and lets you train the squat pattern with heavier loads than any other variation. A good squat is mostly set up before you move: rack height, bar position, grip, bracing and stance. The descent and drive follow the same rules as a bodyweight squat.

name: Bench Press
index_description: Unrack the bar and position it over chest. Lower bar to chest with control, touching lightly at nipple line. Press bar back up to starting position, maintaining tight core and leg drive.

steps.name: Set up
steps.text: Lie flat on bench with eyes under the bar. Plant feet firmly on floor. Grip bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. Retract shoulder blades and maintain arch in lower back.

steps.name: Create a stable start
steps.text: Set the bench and feet firmly, bring the dumbbell or dumbbells into position, and brace before pressing.

steps.name: Perform the movement
steps.text: Unrack the bar and position it over chest. Lower bar to chest with control, touching lightly at nipple line. Press bar back up to starting position, maintaining tight core and leg drive.

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Stack the weight over the shoulder without forcefully clashing the dumbbells or losing rib position.

name: Bodyweight Squat
index_description: Lower your body by pushing hips back and bending knees until thighs are parallel to floor. Drive through heels to return to starting position.

steps.name: Set the feet
steps.text: Stand with feet about shoulder width, toes turned out 10-30 degrees. Feel the heel, big toe and little toe pressing into the floor.

steps.name: Brace
steps.text: Take a breath into the belly and tighten the trunk as if preparing to be pushed.

steps.name: Sit down between the hips
steps.text: Bend the hips and knees at the same time. Let the knees travel forward and follow the direction of the toes.

steps.name: Reach depth
steps.text: Go at least until the thighs are parallel to the floor, or as deep as you can keep the heels down and the back neutral.

steps.name: Stand up
steps.text: Push the floor away and straighten the hips and knees together. Finish standing tall without leaning back.

instructions:
1. Set the feet: Stand with feet about shoulder width, toes turned out 10-30 degrees. Feel the heel, big toe and little toe pressing into the floor.
2. Brace: Take a breath into the belly and tighten the trunk as if preparing to be pushed.
3. Sit down between the hips: Bend the hips and knees at the same time. Let the knees travel forward and follow the direction of the toes.

5. Stand up: Push the floor away and straighten the hips and knees together. Finish standing tall without leaning back.

full_description: The butterfly pull-up is a cyclical, high-speed pull-up used in CrossFit. steps.name: Protract and lock
steps.text: Push the floor away so the shoulder blades spread, and lock the elbows.

steps.name: Lean
steps.text: Lean forward until the shoulders are well past the hands.

steps.name: Lift into the line
steps.text: Lift the legs straight back so the body is one line parallel to the floor.

steps.name: Hold
steps.text: Hold only while the elbows stay locked and the hips stay level.

Piked or sagging hips.
Skipping progressions and wrist preparation.

full_description: The full planche is a horizontal hold above the floor on straight arms, with the body straight and the legs together. It is among the hardest calisthenics skills and typically takes years of consistent training. The progression runs through planche leans, tuck, advanced tuck, single-leg or straddle, and finally the full planche.

name: Pull-Up
index_description: Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar, then lower yourself back to the starting position with control

steps.name: Grip the bar
steps.text: Hang with an overhand grip just outside shoulder width, thumbs wrapped around the bar.

steps.name: Start from an active hang
steps.text: From straight arms, pull the shoulder blades down and slightly back so the shoulders move away from the ears. This small movement starts every rep.

steps.name: Pull the elbows down
steps.text: Drive the elbows down toward the ribs while the chest rises toward the bar. Keep the legs together and slightly in front of you.

steps.name: Clear the bar
steps.text: Finish when the chin is clearly over the bar without tipping the head back.

steps.name: Lower all the way
steps.text: Lower over 2-3 seconds to straight arms. Partial reps that stop short of straight elbows do not count.

instructions:
1. Grip the bar: Hang with an overhand grip just outside shoulder width, thumbs wrapped around the bar.
2. Start from an active hang: From straight arms, pull the shoulder blades down and slightly back so the shoulders move away from the ears. This small movement starts every rep.
3. Pull the elbows down: Drive the elbows down toward the ribs while the chest rises toward the bar. Keep the legs together and slightly in front of you.
4. Clear the bar: Finish when the chin is clearly over the bar without tipping the head back.
5. Lower all the way: Lower over 2-3 seconds to straight arms. Partial reps that stop short of straight elbows do not count.
common_mistakes: Kipping or kicking the legs to get over the bar.
Starting each rep with bent elbows and never reaching a full hang.
Craning the chin up to the bar while the body stays low.
Dropping quickly on the way down and losing the strength-building lowering phase.
Training to failure every set, which reduces the number of quality reps you can do in a week.
easier_variations: Band-Assisted Pull-up:A band reduces the load most at the bottom.
Assisted Pull-up:A machine provides constant, adjustable assistance.
Negative Pull-up:Build strength in the lowering phase.
harder_variations: Weighted Pull-up:Add load once 10+ strict reps are reliable.
L-Sit Pull-up:Hold the legs at 90 degrees to add trunk demand and remove the kick.
Archer Pull-up:Shift the load toward one arm on the way to a one-arm pull-up.

programming.Strength: 4-6 sets of 3-6 repetitions with 2-3 minutes rest, stopping 1-2 reps before failure.
programming.Muscle growth: 3-4 sets of 6-12 repetitions close to failure, 2-3 sessions per week, counting toward roughly 10+ weekly sets for the back.
programming.Building your first pull-ups: Train vertical pulling 3 times per week with assisted reps and negatives, and test strict reps every 2-3 weeks.

full_description: A pull-up is a vertical pull from a dead hang to chin over the bar with an overhand grip. It is one of the most useful bodyweight strength tests, and also one of the most commonly cheated. A strict rep starts from straight arms, keeps the legs quiet and finishes with the chin over the bar, not just reaching for it.

name: Push-Up

steps.name: Place the hands
steps.text: Put the hands slightly wider than shoulder width, roughly under the shoulders, fingers spread and pointing forward.

steps.name: Make a straight line
steps.text: Walk the feet back into a plank. Squeeze the glutes and brace the abs so the head, hips and heels are in one line.

steps.name: Lower
steps.text: Bend the elbows, keeping them at roughly 30-60 degrees from the torso, until the chest is a fist's width from the floor.

full_description: A push-up is a horizontal press in which you lower your chest toward the floor from a straight-arm plank and press back up. It requires no equipment, scales from wall push-ups to one-arm push-ups, and research shows that challenging push-up variations can build strength as effectively as the bench press.

name: Wall Handstand
index_description: Kick up to handstand position with feet resting against wall for support, maintain straight line

steps.name: Chest-to-wall entry
steps.text: Start in a plank with feet at the wall, walk the feet up the wall while walking the hands toward it until the body is nearly vertical.

steps.name: Hand distance
steps.text: Aim for hands about 10-20 cm from the wall.

steps.name: Line up
steps.text: Push tall through the shoulders, squeeze the glutes, and point the toes.

steps.name: Hold
steps.text: Hold for 20-60 seconds.

steps.name: Exit
steps.text: Walk the hands out and feet down, or cartwheel out.

instructions:

Holding the breath.

programming.Progression rule: Move on when you can hold the current variation for 3 sets of 20-30 seconds with a straight line.

full_description: A wall handstand uses the wall for balance so you can build shoulder strength and a straight body line upside down. There are two versions: chest-to-wall, where you walk your feet up the wall facing it, and back-to-wall, where you kick up with your back to the wall. Chest-to-wall teaches a straighter line.

name: Weighted Front Lever
index_description: From hanging position, raise weighted body to horizontal position. Maintain front lever form despite added resistance.

steps.name: Check prerequisites
steps.text: Be able to hold a full front lever for 5 sets of 8-12 seconds with locked elbows and level hips.

steps.name: Choose the load
steps.text: Start with the smallest practical load; a close-fitting vest is easier to control than ankle weights.

steps.name: Enter and hold
steps.text: Pull into the full lever exactly as you would unweighted and hold for shorter durations.

steps.name: Exit with control
steps.text: Lower slowly to a hang before releasing.

instructions:

common_mistakes: Adding load before the unweighted lever is solid.

Accepting a pike or bent elbows under load.

full_description: A weighted front lever adds external load, usually a vest or ankle weights, to a full front lever. steps.text: Hold your unweighted planche variation for several sets of 5-10 seconds.

steps.name: Choose the load

steps.name: Hold

instructions:

full_description: A weighted planche adds a vest or ankle weights to a full or straddle planche. It is for advanced athletes who already hold clean planches for multiple sets. Ankle weights are much harder than a vest because they load the end of the lever.

name: Weighted Pull-up
index_description: Pull your body and the additional weight up until chin clears the bar, then lower with control

steps.name: Set up
steps.text: Attach additional weight using a weight belt or weighted vest, then hang from the pull-up bar with proper grip

steps.name: Create a stable start
steps.text: Take a secure grip and begin from a controlled hang with the shoulder blades gently active.

steps.name: Perform the movement
steps.text: Pull your body and the additional weight up until chin clears the bar, then lower with control

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Reach the strongest height you can without craning the neck, then return to a full controlled hang.

Dropping through the eccentric

full_description: Weighted Pull-up is a advanced pull exercise for vertical pulling strength through the back, arms, and shoulder girdle. The source muscle map identifies Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps Brachii Long Head, Biceps Brachii Short Head as the primary targets.

name: Weighted Push-up
index_description: Lower chest toward floor while maintaining weight position, then push back up to starting position.

steps.name: Set up
steps.text: Place weight on upper back/shoulders. Assume standard push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulders.

steps.name: Create a stable start
steps.text: Place the hands securely, spread the fingers, and establish a rigid line through the head, ribs, pelvis, and legs.

steps.name: Perform the movement
steps.text: Lower chest toward floor while maintaining weight position, then push back up to starting position.

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Press the floor away until the elbows are straight without letting the hips sag or lead the movement.

name: Weighted Sit-Up
index_description: Contract your abs and lift your torso up while keeping the weight secure against your chest. Pause at the top, then slowly lower back down.

steps.name: Choose and position the load
steps.text: Start with a 2.5-10 kg plate or a light dumbbell. Lie on your back with knees bent at about 90 degrees and hold the weight flat against your upper chest with both hands, close to the sternum.

steps.name: Set the feet
steps.text: Keep both feet flat. Anchoring the feet under a pad makes the lift easier but shifts more work to the hip flexors; leave them free if your goal is abdominal strength and you can complete the reps.

steps.name: Curl, then sit
steps.text: Exhale and curl the head, shoulders and ribs off the floor first, then continue up until your torso is roughly upright. The weight should travel with your chest, not drift forward.

steps.name: Pause at the top
steps.text: Hold for one second without leaning back against the weight. If you need to swing the plate to get up, the load is too heavy.

steps.name: Lower one segment at a time
steps.text: Take 2-3 seconds to roll back down, lower back first and head last. Touch the floor lightly and start the next repetition without bouncing.

instructions:
1. Choose and position the load: Start with a 2.5-10 kg plate or a light dumbbell. Lie on your back with knees bent at about 90 degrees and hold the weight flat against your upper chest with both hands, close to the sternum.
2. Set the feet: Keep both feet flat. Anchoring the feet under a pad makes the lift easier but shifts more work to the hip flexors; leave them free if your goal is abdominal strength and you can complete the reps.
3. Curl, then sit: Exhale and curl the head, shoulders and ribs off the floor first, then continue up until your torso is roughly upright. The weight should travel with your chest, not drift forward.
4. Pause at the top: Hold for one second without leaning back against the weight. If you need to swing the plate to get up, the load is too heavy.
5. Lower one segment at a time: Take 2-3 seconds to roll back down, lower back first and head last. Touch the floor lightly and start the next repetition without bouncing.
coaching_cues: Ribs to hips, then sit tall
common_mistakes: Holding the weight away from the chest by accident: the longer lever can double the difficulty mid-set.
Yanking the head forward with the chin, which strains the neck without adding abdominal work.
Dropping back to the floor and bouncing out of the bottom instead of controlling the lowering phase.
Choosing a load that requires a jerk or a foot anchor to finish the repetition.
Adding load before you can do 15 smooth bodyweight sit-ups.
easier_variations: Incline Sit-up:Reduces the range against gravity while keeping the full movement.
Banded Sit-up:A band anchored behind you can assist the hardest part of the range.
harder_variations: Weight held at arm's length:Pressing the plate toward the ceiling lengthens the lever without adding kilograms.
Decline Sit-up:A decline bench increases the range worked against gravity.
Leg raises:Moves the challenge to the lower trunk and hip flexors while hanging.

programming.Strength: 3-4 sets of 6-10 controlled repetitions with a load that leaves 1-3 repetitions in reserve. Rest 90-120 seconds.
programming.Muscle growth: 2-4 sets of 8-15 repetitions taken close to failure, 2-3 times per week as part of roughly 10+ weekly sets for the trunk flexors.
programming.Technique and tolerance: 2-3 sets of 5-8 slow repetitions with a 3-second lowering phase before adding load or range.

full_description: A weighted sit-up is a full sit-up performed while holding a plate, dumbbell or kettlebell against the chest. The added load lets you keep the repetition range moderate as your abdominal strength improves, instead of piling up dozens of bodyweight reps. Where you hold the weight changes the difficulty more than how heavy it is.

name: Wide Stance Squat

steps.name: Create a stable start

steps.name: Perform the movement

steps.name: Finish with control
steps.text: Stand by driving the floor away and extending the hips and knees together without shifting onto the toes.

steps.text: Stack the weight over the shoulder without forcefully clashing the dumbbells or losing rib position.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up

steps.text: Grip about 1.5 times shoulder width. If your shoulders feel pinched, bring the hands in.

steps.name: Set the shoulders
steps.text: From straight arms, depress the shoulder blades before bending the elbows.

steps.name: Pull to the upper chest
steps.text: Drive the elbows down and out until the chin clears the bar.

steps.name: Lower fully
steps.text: Lower to straight arms over 2-3 seconds.

instructions:

full_description: A wide-grip pull-up uses an overhand grip noticeably wider than the shoulders, usually about 1.5 times shoulder width. The wider grip shortens the range of motion and puts the shoulders in a more abducted position, and most people can do fewer reps than with a standard grip. Wider is not automatically better: choose a width that is comfortable for your shoulders.
